findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
findings.body: The fourth `Objects.requireNonNull` call checks `grantType` again but uses the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed". `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null raw ID is therefore accepted silently, and `encodeTokenId` would produce an ID like `onrtac:null` instead of failing fast. The call should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong offset and inverted condition
findings.body: The grant shortcut occupies characters 4..6 of the prefix (e.g. `ac` in `onrtac`), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is the `ta` in `onrtac`. It also returns false when the substring *equals* the expected shortcut, so the check is inverted. In practice the extracted value almost never equals the shortcut, so the matcher accepts any grant type. The new event assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken therefore do not verify the encoded grant type at all. The check should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, ideally with a length check on `items[0]` first.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks custom grant type providers; javadoc contradicts required length
findings.body:
`getShortcut()` is added as an abstract interface method. Every existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation will fail to compile, or throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls it. A default implementation would avoid this.

The javadoc also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but the decoder requires exactly a 6-character prefix, i.e. a 2-character grant shortcut. A custom grant following the docs would issue tokens whose IDs cannot be decoded: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` throws "Expected length of 6". Shortcut length is not validated anywhere.

findings.title: Offline-token flows encode session type as online
findings.body:
The session type comes from `userSession.isOffline()` at the time the access token is created. In `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` and the ROPC grant, the access token is created before `generateRefreshToken()`. That call creates the offline session, and the online session is then removed when FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS is set or for direct grants.

As a result, the access token issued with an offline token is encoded `on`, while the online session it refers to is deleted. The stated goal of using the session type to look up only one session type (#37662) would then fail to find the session for these tokens.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context removed
findings.body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor is removed without replacement. Extensions or custom grant types that wrap or copy the context will break. Removing it is unrelated to the feature. If it is kept, it should also copy the new `grantType` field.

findings.title: Lazy refresh of grant shortcuts skips duplicate validation and can fail token issuance
findings.body:
`postInit` validates that grant shortcuts are unique. The runtime refresh paths in `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` do not. A hot-deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the `grantsByShortcuts` entry, so existing tokens decode to the wrong grant type.

Separately, any code path that sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to a value with no registered factory now makes `initToken` throw `IllegalStateException`. Token issuance fails outright instead of degrading to the unknown (`na`) value.
